newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC hits all-time high ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: HSBC hits all-time high ahead of results.

text.p: Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc hit an all-time high on Tuesday ahead of the release of its 1996 results next Monday and after the bank's Canadian unit posted 28 percent net earnings growth in the first quarter, brokers said.
The stock was the most actively traded during the afternoon and rose HK$5.50, or 2.92 percent, to HK$194 before falling back slightly to HK$193.50.
Volume was 3.95 million shares worth HK$756.47 million.
"Expectations that the bank will post strong yearly earnings after the bank's Canadian unit posted satisfactory results fueled buying," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Hong Kong Bank of Canada, an indirectly wholly-owned unit of HSBC, posted a 28 percent rise in net profit to C$31.0 million for the first quarter ended January 31.
Brokers said it was a good sign and the market generally expected a strong performance for the whole group.

"Buying interest (from overseas investors) is still there," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "The market is generally expecting HSBC shares to hit a short-term target of HK$200 some time before or after the earnings report."
